cards.title: Researchers show how JEPAs can align image and text representations
cards.summary: Randall Balestriero and Yann LeCun present a theorem about models trained separately on different kinds of data. They say joint-embedding predictive architectures, or JEPAs, learn matching representations, apart from a rotation, when each training pair shows the same scene. In tests, these pairs needed 42 times fewer samples than next-token prediction to reach the same alignment. Their 109M-parameter text JEPA aligned with image encoders better than the language models they tested, including models with up to 72B parameters.
cards.reason: The tracked paper page presents a theoretical and empirical result on cross-modal alignment with joint-embedding predictive architectures.

sources.title: Paper page - Proving and Improving the Platonic Representation Hypothesis with JEPAs

cards.title: Tencent researchers introduce Youtu-Parsing-Omni for documents, images, audio and video
cards.summary: Tencent researchers present Youtu-Parsing-Omni, a model that turns documents, images, audio and video into structured records. It uses one shared encoder and one output schema for ten parsing tasks. Video frames can also connect with audio from the same moment. The single 5B-parameter model scored 96.96 overall on OmniDocBench v1.6 and 75.08 on OmniParsingBench, where it led open-weight models. The researchers say its strongest advantage was on audio and video. They made its code and model weights public.
cards.reason: The tracked paper page reports a unified multimodal parsing method and strong results across document, audio, and video benchmarks.

sources.title: Paper page - Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities

cards.title: Jayden Teoh proposes Soft-MTP to improve multi-token prediction
cards.summary: Jayden Teoh identifies a noisy part of the training signal used in standard multi-token prediction. Soft-MTP removes that part and keeps a signal that guides predictions toward the model’s own next-token predictions. Teoh says the change needs no new parameters or measurable extra computing time. In tests on models from 167M to 1.2B parameters, Soft-MTP improved next-token perplexity, speculative decoding speed and zero-shot accuracy at every size. At 1.2B parameters, it also improved math and code reasoning after fine-tuning.
cards.reason: The tracked paper page proposes a low-overhead training change that improves multi-token prediction and speculative decoding.

sources.title: Paper page - Multi-Token Prediction Done Right

cards.title: Researchers introduce SpecSlot to generate detailed images with less computation
cards.summary: Jiongfan Yang and colleagues introduce SpecSlot, a method for generating images directly in pixel space. It divides each image area into slots for different levels of detail. Only the slots for broad image structure exchange information across the whole image. Detail slots interact locally. On ImageNet-512, SpecSlot improved FID by 2.84 against a control model while using 3.9% less computation. It came within 0.69 FID of JiT-B/16 at 38.2% lower cost. It also beat JiT-B/8 on a text-to-image benchmark.
cards.reason: The tracked paper page introduces a more compute-efficient tokenization method for pixel-space image generation.

sources.title: Paper page - Read, Allocate, Route: Role-Coupled Tokenization for Pixel-Space Generative Transformers

cards.title: Researchers test AI investment agents with Investor’s Last Exam
cards.summary: Researchers introduce Investor’s Last Exam to test whether AI agents can research stocks and make forecasts using only information available at decision time. Experienced investors and fund managers helped lead the benchmark. Its database contains 3.43 million document versions, and its evaluation covers 86 assignments. GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 scored 68.1 and 66.9 out of 100 overall. Astra scored 52.5 on Forecast & Model. The researchers say strong research results did not translate into equally strong forecasts and investment judgments.
cards.reason: The tracked paper page introduces an equity-research agent benchmark and identifies gaps between research quality and forecasting.

sources.title: Paper page - Investor's Last Exam: Can AI Agents Do Equity Investment Without Seeing the Future?

cards.title: Researchers introduce WebAnything to rebuild websites for agent training
cards.summary: Tianci Xie and colleagues present WebAnything, a system that builds reusable website environments from real URLs. It collects browser-visible structures and interaction results, then uses an independent verifier to check and repair each copy. The researchers built 244 website artifacts across 14 application domains and 53 categories. These supported 12,984 accepted tasks. In a blind audit against WebHarbor, WebAnything recorded 12 wins, two ties and no losses. Training Qwen3.5-9B on 5,856 interaction histories improved its success on several web-agent tests.
cards.reason: The tracked paper page describes a method for reconstructing reusable web-agent environments and reports improved agent performance.

sources.title: Paper page - WebAnything: From the Wild Web to Scalable Agent Environments

cards.title: Researchers make one Glance model rank passages and answer questions
cards.summary: Adilet Metinov and Chingiz Arziev introduce Glance, which lets one 9B model rank source passages and generate answers. A small adapter scores passages from shared cached context, instead of using a separate ranking model. Each decision skill adds about 0.1 GiB of memory. After 39 minutes of training, Glance scored 0.741 on SciFact and 0.345 on NFCorpus, above the comparison reranker’s 0.721 and 0.326. On 300 HotpotQA questions, its chosen passages improved answer F1 by 0.045. The study used one model family.
cards.reason: The tracked paper page evaluates a method for combining retrieval reranking and generation in one model backbone.

sources.title: Paper page - Glance: The Generator Is Its Own Reranker

cards.title: OpenAI announces new ChatGPT protections for teens and safety reporting
cards.summary: OpenAI says it is strengthening violence prevention in ChatGPT. The announcement includes expanded safeguards and earlier interventions. It also introduces new protections for teens and a commitment to public safety reporting. These measures concern safety in ChatGPT and how OpenAI reports on that work. The provided announcement does not describe the individual safeguards or say when each change will take effect. It also does not give figures for how often the new protections will intervene.
cards.reason: OpenAI is introducing expanded ChatGPT safeguards and earlier interventions for teen and violence-related safety.

sources.title: Community safety report and new protections for teens

cards.title: Tencent researchers introduce WeVisCut to turn narration into long videos
cards.summary: Tencent researchers present WeVisCut, a system that uses one 9B model to coordinate tools for making long videos from narration. Its agent uses tool feedback to guide later editing steps and repair failures. The researchers used 3,750 finished videos to create 134,771 training examples. On a 100-task benchmark, WeVisCut achieved a 90.5 overall score. Under the same tool conditions, its performance was comparable to Claude Opus 5 while it generated about 33 times fewer tokens per successful output minute.
cards.reason: The tracked paper page describes a trained long-form video-editing agent and reports benchmark and efficiency results.

sources.title: Paper page - WeVisCut: The Whole Editing Room in One Agent From Narration to Long-Form Video

cards.title: Amazon adds GPT-5.6 APIs and cross-region routing to Bedrock
cards.summary: Amazon says Bedrock now supports OpenAI GPT-5.6 Terra and Luna through its bedrock-runtime endpoint in AWS GovCloud (US). Customers can use the Responses, Converse and Chat Completions APIs. Cross-Region Inference routes requests across both AWS GovCloud (US) Regions to increase available throughput and redundancy while maintaining US data sovereignty. The APIs also use Bedrock’s existing account controls, including invocation logs, CloudWatch metrics and itemized cost reports. Amazon says cross-region inference for OpenAI models is available in every AWS Region that offers those models on Bedrock.
cards.reason: Amazon Bedrock is adding cross-region inference and expanded API support for OpenAI models in AWS GovCloud.

sources.title: Amazon Bedrock expands API support and introduces Cross-Region Inferencing for OpenAI models in AWS GovCloud (US)

cards.title: Microsoft built synthetic enterprise environments to test Copilot
cards.summary: Microsoft built the Industry Evaluation Data Generation Platform to test Copilot without using customer data. It creates synthetic workplaces with users, meetings, emails, documents, and organizational structures. Public sources, including O*NET occupational data, online job postings, and SEC filings, help ground these environments. The platform also generates test queries and uses quality checks to assess the data. Automated content-safety checks aim to keep harmful and personally identifiable material out of the generated data. Microsoft says realistic workflows can reveal issues that generic benchmarks miss.
cards.reason: Microsoft describes a synthetic enterprise-data generation and evaluation method for testing Copilot without customer data.

sources.title: From synthetic enterprise data evaluations to real Microsoft Copilot AI confidence

cards.title: CoSTA researchers compressed speech tokens to speed spoken dialogue models
cards.summary: Researchers introduced CoSTA, a method that changes how spoken dialogue models generate speech tokens. It compresses the tokens used during generation, then expands them into the original token space before speech synthesis. The method keeps the existing speech tokenizer and decoder. On Chinese and English speech-dialogue benchmarks, CoSTA produced expanded speech tokens about 1.7 times faster. The researchers also report lower full-response latency and higher throughput while preserving response quality. Their tests suggest the method can work across model architectures.
cards.reason: The tracked paper page presents a speech-token adaptation method with reported dialogue-inference speed gains.

sources.title: Paper page - CoSTA: Compressed Speech Token Adaptation for Efficient Spoken Dialogue Models

cards.title: IntReal researchers released data and tests for mixed text-image generation
cards.summary: Researchers introduced IntReal to study models that generate text and images in an alternating sequence. It includes IntReal-100K, a real-world dataset spanning four major categories, and an evaluation suite that measures seven performance dimensions. The suite agreed with human judgments at 83.3% accuracy in the researchers’ tests. Tests across four model families revealed different strengths and weaknesses. The researchers also report that training with IntReal-100K improved mixed text-image generation. Training on one type of output alone could help too.
cards.reason: The tracked paper page introduces and validates a benchmark for interleaved text-and-image generation.

sources.title: Paper page - IntReal: A Real-World Dataset and Benchmark for Multimodal Interleaved Generation

cards.title: OpenAI said it will honor a shared website training-preference signal
cards.summary: OpenAI says it will honor a shared robots.txt signal for AI training preferences. The signal is intended to help website operators communicate their preferences to participating providers. Website operators would express the preference through robots.txt, and participating providers could receive that shared signal. OpenAI describes its own commitment in future terms: it will honor the signal. The announcement concerns a way for websites to state their AI training preferences. It does not say that every provider will participate.
cards.reason: OpenAI is adding a way for websites to communicate AI training preferences through a shared robots.txt signal.

sources.title: Making it easier for websites to express AI training preferences

cards.title: Amazon SageMaker AI added GPU partitioning for real-time endpoints
cards.summary: Amazon SageMaker AI inference now lets customers divide one GPU among several models at a real-time endpoint. NVIDIA Multi-Instance GPU technology creates as many as seven isolated partitions, each with its own memory and compute. Customers can size a partition for each model instead of assigning each model an entire GPU. Hardware isolation prevents a busy model from taking memory or throughput from its neighbors. Customers configure partitioning when they create an endpoint and still invoke each model by name, without changing application code.
cards.reason: SageMaker AI is adding GPU partitioning for real-time inference endpoints so multiple models can share an accelerator.

sources.title: Amazon SageMaker AI inference now supports GPU partitioning for real-time endpoints

cards.title: AMD released inference support for five MONAI medical imaging models
cards.summary: AMD released Early Access inference support for five MONAI Model Zoo bundles on AMD Instinct GPUs as part of AMD Life Science 26.08. The bundles cover tasks including whole-body and pancreas CT segmentation and interactive annotation. A ROCm configuration overlay applies optimizations without changing model weights or inference logic. AMD says all five bundles meet their upstream Dice accuracy thresholds. On an Instinct MI355X with ROCm 10.0, AMD measured compiled-PyTorch latencies from 3.60 milliseconds to 3,287 milliseconds across the bundles.
cards.reason: AMD is releasing validated, optimized inference support for five MONAI Model Zoo bundles on Instinct GPUs.

sources.title: Bringing the MONAI Model Zoo to AMD Instinct™ GPUs: Validated Inference on ROCm
